'''Marni Lynn von Wilpert'''<ref name="von Wilpert attorney license">{{cite web |title=State Bar of California Licensee Detail - Marni von Wilpert |url=https://apps.calbar.ca.gov/attorney/Licensee/Detail/321447 |access-date=December 11, 2024 |website=State Bar of California |language=en-US}}</ref> (born December 27, 1982)<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2019 |title=marni_von_wilpert |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/B6mEKQ7HQ0h/ |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=[[Instagram]]}}</ref> is an American attorney and politician who is the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative-elect]] for [[California's 48th congressional district]].<ref name="SDUT North County Race" /> 

A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], she has served as a member of the [[San Diego City Council]] since 2020, representing [[San Diego City Council#District 5|District 5]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Councilmember Marni von Wilpert (District 5) {{!}} City of San Diego Official Website |url=https://www.sandiego.gov/citycouncil/cd5 |access-date=December 11, 2024 |website=www.sandiego.gov}}</ref>  Prior to her election to the council, von Wilpert worked as an attorney for the [[National Labor Relations Board]], on the staff of the [[United States House Committee on Education and Workforce|House Education and Labor Committee]], and as San Diego Deputy City Attorney.

== Early life and career ==
Marni von Wilpert was born and raised in the [[Scripps Ranch, San Diego|Scripps Ranch]] neighborhood of [[San Diego]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SR residents compete in District 5 race|url=http://www.scrippsranchnews.com/news/fullstory.php?ID=1913|access-date=2020-12-13|website=www.scrippsranchnews.com}}</ref> After graduating from [[Scripps Ranch High School]] in 2001, she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in peace and conflict studies from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2005.<ref name="Von Wilpert LinkedIn">{{Cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/marni-von-wilpert-86218311/ |title=Marni von Wilpert |publisher=[[LinkedIn]] |access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref> She then served as a [[Peace Corps]] volunteer in [[Botswana]] from 2006 to 2008, during the height of the [[HIV/AIDS in Africa|HIV/AIDS epidemic in Africa]].<ref name="KPBS Von Wilpert Lead Levanthal D5">{{Cite web|last=Trageser|first=Claire|title=Von Wilpert Leading Levanthal In Race For San Diego City Council District 5 Seat|url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/2020/nov/03/matter-leventhal-von-wilpert-vying-san-diego-city-/|access-date=2020-12-13|website=KPBS Public Media|date=4 November 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

Von Wilpert obtained a [[Juris Doctor]] from the [[Fordham University School of Law]] in 2011.<ref name="Von Wilpert LinkedIn" /><ref name="KPBS Von Wilpert Lead Levanthal D5" /> After graduating from law school, von Wilpert founded a legal clinic associated with the Mississippi Center for Justice.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-05-22|title=Teen Health Mississippi Hires Executive Director|url=https://apnews.com/press-release/BusinessWire/796f00a6e0e74ad0b9f87e21b7a8714e|access-date=2021-01-13|website=AP NEWS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=6 September 2012|title=Marni von Wilpert|url=https://aids.harvard.edu/tag/marni-von-wilpert/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-12-13|website=Harvard AIDS Initiative|language=en-us}}</ref> During her time working in the center's [[Mississippi Delta]] office, she represented people with [[HIV/AIDS]] facing discrimination in both employment and healthcare.<ref name="TOSD How MVW Went to Fav" /> Additionally, von Wilpert served as a [[law clerk]] for Judge [[James E. Graves Jr.]] and worked as an attorney for the [[National Labor Relations Board]]. She was also a detail staffer on the [[United States House Committee on Education and Labor]] and served as an advisor to committee chair Congressman [[Bobby Scott (politician)|Bobby Scott]]. While a part of the committee staff, von Wilpert helped to draft labor legislation that included the [[Protecting the Right to Organize Act]].<ref name="TOSD How MVW Went to Fav" /> In 2017, von Wilpert joined the [[Economic Policy Institute]] as Associate Labor Counsel.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Testimony for New York City Council Committee on Civil Service and Labor|url=https://www.epi.org/publication/testimony-for-new-york-city-council-committee-on-civil-service-and-labor/|access-date=2021-01-13|website=Economic Policy Institute|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marni von Wilpert|url=https://www.epi.org/people/marni-von-wilpert/|access-date=2020-12-13|website=Economic Policy Institute|language=en-US}}</ref> She served as Deputy City Attorney in the [[San Diego City Attorney]]'s Office from 2018 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-10|title=Marni von Wilpert officially joins the San Diego City Council|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/pomerado-news/rancho-bernardo/story/2020-12-10/marni-von-wilpert-officially-joins-the-san-diego-city-council|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-12-13|website=Pomerado News|language=en-US}}</ref>

== San Diego City Council ==
=== Elections ===
{{main|2020 San Diego elections#District 5|2024 San Diego elections#District 5}}
In the [[2020 San Diego elections|2020 San Diego city council election]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2020-10-22|title=Ethics complaints bring new controversy to key San Diego council runoff|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/politics/story/2020-10-22/ethics-complaints-bring-new-controversy-to-key-san-diego-council-runoff|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-13|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}}</ref> von Wilpert placed first in the [[nonpartisan blanket primary]] and defeated Joe Leventhal in the November general election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marni von Wilpert|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Marni_von_Wilpert|access-date=2020-12-13|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}}</ref> She assumed office on December 10, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-07|title=Von Wilpert brings to council hands-on experience that fits with San Diego's challenges|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/politics/story/2020-12-06/von-wilpert-brings-hands-on-experience-to-san-diego-council-that-fits-with-citys-challenges|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-12-13|website=San Diego Union-Tribune|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=They Checked Out Pride Books in Protest. It Backfired. (Published 2023) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/22/us/pride-books-library-protest.html |access-date=2025-11-12 |language=en}}</ref>  She ran unopposed in the [[2024 San Diego City Council election]], winning reelection outright in the primary on March 5, 2024.<ref name="2024 Primary results">{{cite web|url=https://www.livevoterturnout.com/ENR/sandiegocaenr/19/en/Index_19.html|title= San Diego County Primary Election Results, March 5, 2024|author=<!--Not stated-->|date=April 4, 2024|website=|publisher=|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref>

=== Tenure ===
During her first term, she was appointed to serve on the San Diego County Regional Airport Authority board of directors in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Mayor Gloria announces appointments to Airport Authority Board - Mayor Todd Gloria|url=http://www.sdnews.com/view/full_story/27786987/article-Mayor-Gloria-announces-appointments-to-Airport-Authority-Board-|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-13|website=www.sdnews.com}}</ref> Von Wilpert voted for a city council ordinance in 2023 that permitted police to remove homeless encampments on public property if city shelter beds were available, which passed in a 5–4 vote.<ref name="KPBS encampment ban passes">{{cite news|author=City News Service|date=June 13, 2024 |title=San Diego City Council approves Unsafe Camping Ordinance by 5-4 vote|url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/local/2023/06/14/san-diego-city-council-approves-unsafe-camping-ordinance-homelessness|newspaper=KPBS |location=San Diego, CA|access-date=October 12, 2026}}</ref>

During her second term, von Wilpert co-sponsored an ordinance which required grocery stores with [[Digital coupon|digital-only coupons]] to make the same discounts available to all customers in-store. The measure passed unanimously, making San Diego the first city in the United States to adopt such a requirement.<ref>{{cite news |title=San Diego becomes first city in nation to ban digital-only grocery deals |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/politics/2025/03/24/san-diego-becomes-first-city-in-nation-to-ban-digital-only-grocery-deals |work=Times of San Diego |date=March 24, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-31 |title=Architects of San Diego’s new grocery coupon law tout its potential savings to seniors in Rancho Bernardo |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2025/07/30/architects-of-san-diegos-new-grocery-coupon-law-tout-its-potential-savings-to-seniors-in-rancho-bernardo/ |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

== U.S. House of Representatives ==
=== Elections ===
{{main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California (districts 27–52)#District 48}}
After her reelection in 2024, von Wilpert filed to run for [[California's 40th State Senatorial district]] in the 2026 election.<ref name="Cst News 3 candidates vying">{{cite news |last=Place |first=Leo |date=January 21, 2025 |title=Three candidates vying for 40th state Senate seat in 2026 |url=https://thecoastnews.com/three-candidates-vying-for-40th-state-senate-seat-in-2026/ |access-date=February 25, 2025 |newspaper=The Coast News Group |location=San Marcos, CA |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Fox 5 SD von Wilpert state senate run">{{Cite web |last=Dawson |first=Danielle |date=September 24, 2024 |title=City Councilmember Marni von Wilpert sets up run for CA State Senate |url=https://fox5sandiego.com/news/local-news/city-councilmember-marni-von-wilpert-sets-up-run-for-ca-state-senate/ |access-date=December 11, 2024 |website=Fox 5 KUSI News |language=en-US}}</ref> Shortly afterwards, she dropped her bid for state senate to run for U.S. Congress in [[California's 48th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-09-03 |title=San Diego City Councilwoman Marni von Wilpert announces congressional campaign |url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/politics/2025/09/03/san-diego-city-councilwoman-marni-von-wilpert-announces-congressional-campaign |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=KPBS Public Media |language=en}}</ref> During the primary, she was supported by the California Federation of Labor Unions [[AFL-CIO]], the [[San Diego County, California|San Diego]] and [[Imperial County, California|Imperial Counties]] Labor Council AFL-CIO, the [[California Teachers Association]], the [[LGBTQ+ Victory Fund]],<ref name="Victory Fund Endorse von Wilpert">{{Cite web |url=https://victoryfund.org/news/lgbtq-victory-fund-endorses-marni-von-wilpert-for-congress-in-ca-48/ |date=March 5, 2026 |title=LGBTQ+ Victory Fund Endorses Marni von Wilpert for Congress in CA-48 |website=LGBTQ+ Victory Fund |access-date=April 8, 2026 |language=en-US }}</ref> former [[President pro tempore of the California State Senate]] [[Toni Atkins]],<ref name="TOSD How MVW Went to Fav">{{cite news|last=Friedell|first=Dan|date=October 11, 2026 |title=How Marni von Wilpert went from a frustrated first-term councilmember to a favorite in one of the country’s biggest Congressional races |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/politics/2026/10/11/von-wilpert-ca-48-congressional-race-desmond/|newspaper=Times of San Diego|location=San Diego, CA|access-date=October 12, 2026}}</ref> and Representative [[Mark Takano]].<ref name="SDUT North County Race">{{cite news|last=Robinson|first=Lucas|date=April 5, 2026 |title=Could Democrats win all San Diego County’s seats in Congress? That all depends on one North County race|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2026/04/05/could-democrats-win-all-san-diego-countys-seats-in-congress-that-all-depends-on-one-north-county-race/|newspaper=San Diego Union-Tribune|location=San Diego, CA|access-date=April 8, 2026}}{{subscription required}}</ref> Von Wilpert and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[San Diego County Board of Supervisors|County Supervisor]] [[Jim Desmond]] advanced from the June primary with 20.6% and 38.9% of the vote, respectively.<ref name="TOSD How MVW Went to Fav" />

After the primary, the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] added von Wilpert to its "Red to Blue" program that highlights its highest-targeted races while the [[National Republican Congressional Committee]] added Desmond to its list of top priority candidates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Diego |first=Drew Sitton • Times of San |date=2026-06-05 |title=National Democratic committee boosts Von Wilpert as she shifts focus to Desmond in 48th District House race |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/politics/2026/06/04/von-wilpert-desmond-congress-dccc/ |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=Times of San Diego |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Self |first=Zac |date=2026-06-04 |title=National organizers set sights on California's 48th Congressional District |url=https://www.10news.com/americavotes/National-organizers-set-sights-on-California's-48th-Congressional-District |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=ABC 10 News San Diego KGTV |language=en}}</ref> By mid-October, von Wilpert had raised $4.5 million against Desmond's $3 million with outside spending in the race exceeding $6 million overall, mostly in support of von Wilpert.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lathan |first=Nadia |last2=Brennan |first2=Deborah |date=2026-10-20 |title=San Diego’s House candidates are running atypically conventional campaigns |url=https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/10/congress-48-wonwilpert-desmond/ |access-date=2026-11-01 |work=CalMatters |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Von Wilpert identifies as a member of the [[LGBTQ]] community.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hyson |first=Katie |date=2023-10-11 |title=On National Coming Out Day, San Diego City Councilmember Marni von Wilpert shares her story |url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/living/2023/10/11/on-national-coming-out-day-san-diego-city-councilmember-marni-von-wilpert-shares-her-story |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=KPBS Public Media |language=en}}</ref>
